hub.title: Free Public Data Tables: Population, GDP, Country Codes and More | cv.cm
hub.description: Open data tables you can search, sort and download as CSV: population, GDP, exports, inflation, unemployment, life expectancy for men and women, birth and death rates, land and forest area, CO2 emissions, renewable energy, internet use, ISO country and currency codes, calling codes, time zones, paper sizes and ASCII.
hub.lede: Plain tables of public data from the World Bank, ISO and IANA. Search, sort by any column, or download the CSV. Every table names its source and licence.
about: Each table is a snapshot of an official source, refreshed from that source and dated on the page. Country figures come from the World Bank World Development Indicators (CC BY 4.0). Codes come from the ISO 3166 and ISO 4217 lists and the IANA time zone database.
Numbers are shown in your language, but the CSV files keep raw values and ISO codes, so they open cleanly in Excel, Google Sheets or code.

faq.q: Where does this data come from?
faq.a: Country statistics are from the World Bank World Development Indicators. Country, currency and dialing codes follow ISO 3166, ISO 4217 and the ITU list. Time zones are from the IANA tz database. Paper sizes follow ISO 216, ISO 269, JIS P 0138 and ANSI.

faq.q: Can I use these tables for free?
faq.a: Yes. World Bank data is licensed CC BY 4.0, so credit the World Bank when you reuse it. Codes and reference tables are public facts you can reuse freely.

faq.q: How current are the numbers?
faq.a: Each page shows the date of its snapshot and the year of every value. The World Bank publishes most indicators a year or two after the fact, so a country's latest value can be from an earlier year.

gdp.title: GDP by Country {to}: Ranking of {rows} Economies in US$ | cv.cm
gdp.description: Gross domestic product of {rows} economies in current US dollars, ranked, with share of world GDP. World GDP {world} ({worldYear}). World Bank data, CSV download.
gdp.lede: Nominal GDP of {rows} economies in current US dollars, ranked, with each one's share of the world total. Source: World Bank.
about: GDP is the value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a year. These figures are converted to US dollars at official exchange rates, so currency swings move them even when output does not.
For living standards, compare GDP per capita, or GDP at purchasing power parity, which adjusts for price levels.

faq.q: Why do some countries show an older year?
faq.a: The World Bank only publishes a figure once a country reports it. Each row shows the latest year available, so a few countries lag behind.

Small financial centres and resource exporters often top the list because a large economy is divided among few residents.

about: Life expectancy at birth is the average number of years a newborn would live if the death rates of the year it was born stayed the same for its whole life. It is a summary of current health, not a forecast.

fertility-rate.description: Total fertility rate (births per woman) for {rows} countries, ranked. World average {world} ({worldYear}). Replacement level is about 2.1. World Bank data, CSV download.

about: The total fertility rate is the number of children a woman would have if she lived to the end of her childbearing years and had children at each age at that year's rates.

gdp-ppp-per-capita.name: GDP per capita (PPP) by country
gdp-ppp-per-capita.title: GDP per Capita PPP by Country {to}: {rows} Countries Ranked | cv.cm
gdp-ppp-per-capita.description: GDP per person at purchasing power parity for {rows} countries, ranked, in current international dollars. World average {world} ({worldYear}). World Bank data, CSV download.
gdp-ppp-per-capita.h1: GDP per capita at purchasing power parity, {to} (current international $)
gdp-ppp-per-capita.lede: Output per person for {rows} countries and areas, converted with purchasing power parity so that a dollar buys the same basket of goods everywhere. Ranked from highest to lowest. Source: World Bank.
facts: World average: {world} international dollars per person ({worldYear}).
about: Purchasing power parity (PPP) converts each currency at the rate that buys the same goods and services as one US dollar buys in the United States. It removes most of the effect of price levels, so it compares living standards better than GDP at market exchange rates.

Small financial centres and oil exporters top the list because their output is large next to the number of residents, not because every resident is that rich. Each row shows the latest year the country reported.

faq.q: Which country has the highest GDP per capita at PPP?
faq.a: {top1}, with {v1} international dollars per person in {year1}, followed by {top2} ({v2}).

faq.q: What is the difference between GDP per capita and GDP per capita PPP?
faq.a: Plain GDP per capita uses market exchange rates. The PPP version adjusts for what money buys locally, so poorer countries with low prices rank higher than they do on the nominal list.

faq.q: Which country has the lowest GDP per capita at PPP?
faq.a: In this list, {last}, at {vlast} international dollars per person.

gdp-growth.name: GDP growth rate by country
gdp-growth.title: GDP Growth Rate by Country {to}: Fastest Growing Economies | cv.cm
gdp-growth.description: Annual real GDP growth for {rows} economies, ranked from fastest to slowest. World growth {world}% ({worldYear}). World Bank data, CSV download.
gdp-growth.lede: How much each economy grew in its latest year, after taking out inflation, for {rows} countries and areas. Negative values mean the economy shrank. Source: World Bank.
about: GDP growth is the yearly change in gross domestic product at constant prices, so it measures real output, not price changes. It is based on each country's own currency.
Small economies swing the most: one new oil field, a bad harvest or a war can move growth by ten points in a year. Look at several years before reading a trend.

faq.q: Which country has the fastest growing economy?
faq.a: {top1}, with real GDP growth of {v1}% in {year1}. {top2} was next at {v2}%.

faq.q: How fast is the world economy growing?
faq.a: World GDP grew {world}% in {worldYear}, in real terms.

faq.q: What does negative GDP growth mean?
faq.a: The economy produced less than the year before. Two quarters in a row of decline is the common rule of thumb for a recession. The lowest value in this list is {last}, at {vlast}%.

inflation.name: Inflation rate by country
inflation.title: Inflation Rate by Country {to}: Consumer Prices in {rows} Countries | cv.cm
inflation.description: Annual consumer price inflation for {rows} countries, ranked from highest to lowest. World inflation {world}% ({worldYear}). World Bank data, CSV download.
inflation.h1: Inflation rate by country, {to} (consumer prices, annual %)
inflation.lede: How much the prices of everyday goods and services rose in each country's latest year, for {rows} countries and areas. Negative values are deflation. Source: World Bank, from IMF data.
about: This is the yearly change in the consumer price index (CPI): the cost of a fixed basket of goods and services that a typical household buys. It is the inflation figure most news reports quote.
Most central banks aim for about 2% a year. Rates above 50% a month are called hyperinflation. Some countries publish late, so check the year column.

faq.q: Which country has the highest inflation rate?
faq.a: {top1}, where consumer prices rose {v1}% in {year1}, followed by {top2} ({v2}%).

faq.q: What is the world inflation rate?
faq.a: Consumer prices worldwide rose {world}% in {worldYear}.

faq.q: Which country has the lowest inflation?
faq.a: In this list, {last}, at {vlast}%. A negative number means prices fell.

unemployment.name: Unemployment rate by country
unemployment.title: Unemployment Rate by Country {to}: {rows} Countries Ranked | cv.cm
unemployment.description: Unemployment as a share of the labour force for {rows} countries, ranked, using ILO modelled estimates. World rate {world}% ({worldYear}). World Bank data, CSV download.
unemployment.h1: Unemployment rate by country, {to} (% of labour force)
unemployment.lede: Share of people who want a job and are looking for one but do not have one, for {rows} countries and areas, ranked from highest to lowest. Source: World Bank, from ILO estimates.
about: The International Labour Organization (ILO) counts someone as unemployed if they had no work, were available to work and looked for a job recently. People who have stopped looking are not in the labour force, so they are not counted.
These are modelled estimates that use one definition for every country, so they can differ from the national figures each government publishes.

faq.a: {top1}, at {v1}% of the labour force in {year1}, followed by {top2} ({v2}%).

faq.a: The ILO estimates {world}% for {worldYear}.

faq.q: Which country has the lowest unemployment rate?
faq.a: In this list, {last}, at {vlast}%. Very low rates often mean many people work informally or for family businesses.

land-area.name: Countries by land area
land-area.title: Countries by Land Area {to}: Largest to Smallest in km² | cv.cm
land-area.description: Land area of {rows} countries and areas in square kilometres, ranked, with share of the world's land. World land area {world} km². World Bank data, CSV download.
land-area.lede: Land area of {rows} countries and areas, from largest to smallest, with each one's share of the world's land. Lakes and rivers are not counted. Source: World Bank, from FAO data.
about: Land area is a country's total area minus inland water such as major rivers and lakes. That is why some figures are smaller than the total area you may see elsewhere: Canada, with many lakes, ranks below China and the United States here.
The list covers the economies the World Bank reports on. Antarctica and disputed areas with no single government are not included.

faq.a: {top1}, with {v1} km² of land, followed by {top2} ({v2} km²) and {top3} ({v3} km²).

faq.q: How much land is there on Earth?
faq.a: The World Bank sums the land of all countries to {world} km² ({worldYear}), roughly a quarter of the Earth's surface. Antarctica is not included.

faq.q: What is the smallest country by land area?
faq.a: In this list, {last}, at {vlast} km². Vatican City is smaller but is not in the World Bank data.

population-density.name: Population density by country
population-density.title: Population Density by Country {to}: People per km² | cv.cm
population-density.description: People per square kilometre of land in {rows} countries and areas, ranked from most to least crowded. World average {world} per km². World Bank data, CSV download.
population-density.h1: Population density by country (people per km² of land)
population-density.lede: How many people live on each square kilometre of land, for {rows} countries and areas, ranked from most to least densely populated. Source: World Bank.
facts: Least densely populated in the list: {last} ({vlast}).
about: Population density is mid-year population divided by land area. It is an average over the whole country, so a country with one huge city and a large empty interior can still have a low figure.
City-states and small islands top the list. Among large countries, Bangladesh is the most crowded.

urban-population.title: Urbanization Rate by Country {to}: Urban Population % in {rows} Countries | cv.cm
urban-population.description: Share of the population living in urban areas for {rows} countries, ranked. World urban share {world}% ({worldYear}). World Bank / UN data, CSV download.

facts: World: {world}% of people live in urban areas ({worldYear}).
about: Each country uses its own definition of urban, usually a minimum number of people or a density threshold, so a town in one country may count as a village in another.
City-states and small territories are 100% urban by definition. More than half of the world's people have lived in cities since about 2007.

aged-65-plus.name: Population aged 65+ by country
aged-65-plus.title: Oldest Countries {to}: Population Aged 65 and Over by Country | cv.cm
aged-65-plus.description: Share of the population aged 65 and above for {rows} countries, ranked from oldest to youngest. World {world}% ({worldYear}). World Bank / UN data, CSV download.
aged-65-plus.h1: Population aged 65 and over by country, {to} (% of total)
aged-65-plus.lede: Share of each country's people who are 65 or older, for {rows} countries and areas, ranked from the oldest population to the youngest. Source: World Bank, from UN population estimates.
facts: World: {world}% of people are 65 or older ({worldYear}).
about: The UN calls a country ageing when more than 7% of its people are 65 or older, aged above 14% and super-aged above 20%. Low birth rates and longer lives push the share up.
Gulf states have very low shares because most residents are working-age migrants, not because their own citizens are young.

birth-rate.name: Birth rate by country
birth-rate.title: Birth Rate by Country {to}: Births per 1,000 People in {rows} Countries | cv.cm
birth-rate.description: Crude birth rate, live births per 1,000 people a year, for {rows} countries, ranked. World {world} ({worldYear}). World Bank / UN data, CSV download.
birth-rate.h1: Birth rate by country, {to} (births per 1,000 people)
birth-rate.lede: Live births in a year for every 1,000 people, for {rows} countries and areas, ranked from highest to lowest. Source: World Bank, from UN population estimates.
about: The crude birth rate divides births by the whole population, so it also depends on the age structure: a country with many young adults has more births even when each woman has few children.
To compare how many children women have, use the fertility rate table. Countries with the lowest birth rates also have the oldest populations.

infant-mortality.name: Infant mortality by country
infant-mortality.title: Infant Mortality Rate by Country {to}: {rows} Countries Ranked | cv.cm
infant-mortality.description: Infant deaths before age one per 1,000 live births for {rows} countries, ranked. World rate {world} ({worldYear}). World Bank / UN IGME data, CSV download.
infant-mortality.h1: Infant mortality rate by country, {to} (per 1,000 live births)
infant-mortality.lede: How many babies out of every 1,000 born alive die before their first birthday, for {rows} countries and areas, ranked from highest to lowest. Source: World Bank, from UN IGME estimates.
facts: World: {world} infant deaths per 1,000 live births ({worldYear}).
about: Infant mortality is one of the clearest signs of a health system's reach: most infant deaths come from premature birth, birth complications and infections that clean water, vaccines and trained birth attendants prevent.
The UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation (UN IGME) combines surveys, censuses and civil registration into one comparable series.

faq.a: In this list, {last}, at {vlast} per 1,000 live births.

co2-per-capita.name: CO2 emissions per capita by country
co2-per-capita.title: CO2 Emissions per Capita by Country {to}: {rows} Countries Ranked | cv.cm
co2-per-capita.description: Carbon dioxide emissions per person in tonnes for {rows} countries, ranked from highest to lowest. World average {world} t ({worldYear}). World Bank / EDGAR data, CSV download.
co2-per-capita.h1: CO2 emissions per capita by country, {to} (tonnes per person)

about: The figures count CO2 from burning fossil fuels and from industry such as cement, inside the country's borders. Emissions from land use change and forestry (LULUCF) are left out, and so are emissions from goods a country imports.
Small oil and gas producers top the list because energy-heavy industry is large next to their population. For a country's total share of world emissions, multiply by its population.

electricity-access.title: Access to Electricity by Country {to}: % of Population | cv.cm
electricity-access.description: Share of the population with access to electricity in {rows} countries, ranked. World {world}% ({worldYear}). World Bank data, CSV download.
electricity-access.h1: Access to electricity by country, {to} (% of population)
electricity-access.lede: Share of each country's people who have electricity at home, for {rows} countries and areas, ranked from highest to lowest. Source: World Bank, from household surveys and the IEA.

population-growth.title: Population Growth Rate by Country {to}: {rows} Countries Ranked | cv.cm
population-growth.description: Annual population growth for {rows} countries, ranked from fastest to slowest. World population grew {world}% in {worldYear}. World Bank data, CSV download.
population-growth.lede: How much each country's population grew or shrank in its latest year, for {rows} countries and areas. Negative values mean the population fell. Source: World Bank, from UN estimates.
about: Population growth counts births minus deaths plus people moving in minus people moving out. In small countries and in the Gulf states, migration moves the figure far more than births do.
Many countries in Europe and East Asia now shrink every year because deaths outnumber births and few migrants arrive.

death-rate.lede: Deaths in a year for every 1,000 people, for {rows} countries and areas, ranked from highest to lowest. Source: World Bank, from UN population estimates.
about: The crude death rate depends mostly on age, not on health care. Countries with many old people, such as those in Eastern Europe, have high rates even where people live long lives.
Gulf states have the lowest rates because most residents are young working-age migrants. To compare health, use life expectancy instead.

life-expectancy-male.lede: How many years a newborn boy would live if current death rates held, for {rows} countries and areas, ranked from highest to lowest. Source: World Bank, from UN estimates.

about: Life expectancy at birth is the average number of years a newborn would live if the death rates of its birth year stayed the same for its whole life. It summarises current health, not a forecast.
Women outlive men in almost every country. Part of the gap is biological and part comes from men's higher rates of smoking, drinking, accidents and violence.

facts: World: {world} maternal deaths per 100,000 live births ({worldYear}).
about: A maternal death is the death of a woman while pregnant or within 42 days of the end of a pregnancy, from causes related to it. Severe bleeding, infections and high blood pressure cause most of them, and most can be prevented with skilled care at birth.
These are modelled estimates from the UN Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (MMEIG), which fills gaps where countries do not register every death.

exports.lede: Value of everything each economy sold to the rest of the world, goods and services together, for {rows} countries and areas, ranked, with each one's share of the world total. Source: World Bank.
about: Exports include goods such as cars, phones and oil, and services such as tourism, shipping, software and finance. Values are in current US dollars, so exchange rate swings move them as well as trade does.
Each row shows the latest year the country reported, within the last four years. Re-exports through trade hubs such as Singapore and Hong Kong are counted where they leave.

faq.q: Do exports include services?
faq.a: Yes. This table counts goods and services together, so countries with large tourism, finance or software sectors rank higher than on a goods-only list.

A country that imports more than it exports runs a trade deficit. Compare this table with the exports table to see each country's balance.

Values are at market exchange rates, so high-wage countries look more expensive than the care they buy. Spending more does not always buy longer lives: compare with the life expectancy table.

about: The labour force counts everyone who works for pay or profit, including farming and family businesses, plus people looking for work. Unpaid housework and care are not counted.

Some of the highest rates are in low-income countries where most women farm. Rates are lowest in parts of the Middle East and South Asia. These are ILO modelled estimates that use one definition for every country.

forest-area.lede: Share of each country's land covered by forest, for {rows} countries and areas, ranked from most to least forested. Source: World Bank, from the FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment.
about: The FAO counts land as forest if it covers more than half a hectare with trees taller than 5 metres and a canopy over 10% of the ground. Plantations count; fruit orchards and city parks do not.
Small tropical countries top the list by share. By total area, Russia, Brazil, Canada, the United States and China hold more than half of the world's forest.

faq.q: Which country has the most forest cover?
faq.a: {top1}, where forest covers {v1}% of the land in {year1}, followed by {top2} ({v2}%).

Many of the highest shares are in low-income countries where most households cook with wood, not in countries with the most wind and solar power. The data lags by a few years.

country-codes.name: Country codes (ISO 3166)
country-codes.title: ISO 3166 Country Codes: Alpha-2, Alpha-3 and Numeric List of {rows} Countries | cv.cm
country-codes.description: All {rows} ISO 3166-1 country codes: two-letter (alpha-2), three-letter (alpha-3) and numeric codes, plus internet domain and continent. Searchable, CSV download.
country-codes.lede: Two-letter, three-letter and numeric codes for all {rows} countries and territories in ISO 3166-1, with each one's internet domain and continent.
facts: {rows} countries and territories have an ISO 3166-1 code.
Alpha-2 codes are used for internet domains (.jp, .de) and in language tags (en-US).
Alpha-3 codes appear on passports; numeric codes come from the UN M49 standard.
about: ISO 3166-1 gives every country and many dependent territories three codes. Alpha-2 (US, CN) is the one most systems use. Alpha-3 (USA, CHN) is easier to read. The numeric code (840, 156) works where Latin letters do not.
The UK uses .uk for its internet domain although its ISO code is GB. Names here are in your language.

faq.q: What is the difference between alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes?
faq.a: Alpha-2 codes have two letters (JP) and are used in domains, language tags and most software. Alpha-3 codes have three letters (JPN) and are used on passports and in statistics.

faq.q: How many ISO country codes are there?
faq.a: ISO 3166-1 lists {rows} countries and territories, each with an alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric code.

faq.q: What is the country code for the United Kingdom?
faq.a: GB (alpha-2), GBR (alpha-3) and 826 (numeric). Its internet domain is .uk.

calling-codes.name: International calling codes
calling-codes.title: International Calling Codes: Country Dialing Code List ({rows} Countries) | cv.cm
calling-codes.description: Country calling codes for {rows} countries and territories, from +1 to +998. Search by country or code, with ISO codes. CSV download.
calling-codes.lede: The number to dial after the international prefix (+) to reach each of {rows} countries and territories.
facts: Dial + (or your country's exit code, such as 00 or 011), then the country code, then the number without its leading 0.
+1 is shared by the US, Canada and many Caribbean islands, which add a 3-digit area code.
+7 is shared by Russia and Kazakhstan.
about: Calling codes are assigned by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU-T E.164). Codes are one to three digits long, and some groups of countries share one code.
On a mobile phone, hold 0 to type +. It works from any country, so you do not need to know the local exit code.

faq.q: How do I call another country?
faq.a: Type + (or your exit code, such as 00 in most countries or 011 in the US), the country code, then the local number without its leading 0.

faq.q: Which country is +86?
faq.a: +86 is China. +852 is Hong Kong, +853 Macao and +886 Taiwan.

faq.q: Why do several countries share +1?
faq.a: They are in the North American Numbering Plan. The 3-digit area code after +1 tells you the country.

currency-codes.name: Currency codes (ISO 4217)
currency-codes.title: ISO 4217 Currency Codes: List of {rows} Currencies with Symbols | cv.cm
currency-codes.description: All {rows} active ISO 4217 currency codes with numeric code, symbol, decimal places and the countries that use each one. Searchable, CSV download.
currency-codes.lede: Three-letter codes, numeric codes, symbols and decimal places for the {rows} currencies in ISO 4217, and where each one is used.
facts: ISO 4217 lists {rows} active currency codes, including funds and precious metals.
The first two letters are usually the ISO country code: JPY is Japan's yen.
Codes starting with X are not tied to a country: XAU is gold, XDR is the IMF's special drawing right.
about: Banks, payment systems and accounting software use ISO 4217 codes because symbols are ambiguous: $ is used by more than 20 currencies.
Decimals is the number of minor-unit digits (cents). JPY and KRW have none, and some Gulf currencies have three.

faq.q: What is the currency code for the Chinese yuan?
faq.a: CNY, numeric code 156. Offshore yuan is often quoted as CNH, but that is a market convention, not an ISO code.

faq.q: How many currencies are there?
faq.a: ISO 4217 lists {rows} active codes, including a few funds, precious metals and testing codes.

faq.q: Why does the euro have one code for many countries?
faq.a: EUR is one currency shared by the euro area, so it has one code. The Used in column lists every country and territory that uses it.

time-zones.name: Time zones (IANA)
time-zones.title: List of Time Zones with UTC Offsets ({rows} IANA Time Zones, {year}) | cv.cm
time-zones.description: All {rows} IANA time zones (Asia/Shanghai, America/New_York) with their UTC offsets in January and July {year}, so you can see daylight saving time. CSV download.
time-zones.lede: Every IANA time zone with its UTC offset in January and July {year}. Where the two differ, the zone uses daylight saving time.
facts: {rows} IANA time zone IDs, sorted from west ({west}) to east ({east}).
A zone whose January and July offsets differ observes daylight saving time.
Some zones are offset by 30 or 45 minutes, such as India (UTC+05:30) and Nepal (UTC+05:45).
about: IANA time zone IDs such as Europe/London are what phones, computers and programming languages use. This list follows IANA's zone.tab: one row per country and zone, each carrying that area's daylight saving rules.
Offsets are calculated for 15 January and 15 July {year} from the {tz} tz database. Governments sometimes change their rules at short notice.

faq.q: What time zone is China in?
faq.a: All of China uses China Standard Time, UTC+08:00, all year. The IANA ID is Asia/Shanghai.

faq.q: What is the difference between UTC and GMT?
faq.a: For everyday use they are the same time. UTC is the atomic time standard; GMT is the time zone at 0° longitude, which the UK uses in winter.

faq.q: How many time zones are there?
faq.a: The IANA database used here has {rows} zone IDs. They use fewer than 40 distinct UTC offsets.

paper-sizes.name: Paper sizes
paper-sizes.title: Paper Sizes Chart: A4, A3, B5, Letter in mm, Inches and Pixels | cv.cm
paper-sizes.description: Dimensions of {rows} paper sizes (A0–A10, B, C, JIS B, Letter, Legal) in millimetres, inches and pixels at 300 and 96 DPI. CSV download.
paper-sizes.h1: Paper sizes in mm, inches and pixels
paper-sizes.lede: Width × height of ISO A, B and C sizes, Japanese JIS B sizes and North American sizes, with pixel sizes for printing (300 DPI) and screens (96 DPI).
facts: Each A size is half the one before it: two A4 sheets make one A3.
about: ISO 216 sizes keep the same 1:√2 shape, so a page scales from A4 to A3 or A5 without cropping. A0 has an area of one square metre.
JIS B sizes, common in Japan and China for notebooks and books, are slightly larger than ISO B. JIS B5 is 182 × 257 mm, while ISO B5 is 176 × 250 mm.

faq.q: What is the size of A4 paper?
faq.a: 210 × 297 mm, or 8.27 × 11.69 inches. At 300 DPI that is 2480 × 3508 pixels.

faq.q: What is the difference between A4 and Letter?
faq.a: A4 (210 × 297 mm) is narrower and taller than US Letter (215.9 × 279.4 mm). Most of the world uses A4; the US, Canada and Mexico use Letter.

faq.q: How many pixels do I need to print A4?
faq.a: 2480 × 3508 px for sharp prints at 300 DPI. 1240 × 1754 px (150 DPI) is enough for drafts.

ascii.name: ASCII table
ascii.title: ASCII Table: All 128 Codes in Decimal, Hex, Octal and Binary | cv.cm
ascii.description: Complete ASCII table of all 128 characters with decimal, hexadecimal, octal and binary values and control character names. CSV download.
ascii.lede: All 128 ASCII codes with their decimal, hex, octal and binary values, the character, and the name of each control character.
facts: Codes 0–31 and 127 are control characters; 32–126 are printable.
A is 65 (0x41) and a is 97 (0x61): upper and lower case differ by 32.
about: ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange, 1963) assigns 128 codes to English letters, digits, punctuation and control signals, using 7 bits.
UTF-8 encodes these 128 characters exactly as ASCII does, so every ASCII file is also valid UTF-8.

faq.q: What is the ASCII code for A?
faq.a: Capital A is 65 in decimal, 0x41 in hex and 1000001 in binary. Lowercase a is 97 (0x61).

faq.q: What is the ASCII code for a space?
faq.a: 32 in decimal, 0x20 in hex.

faq.q: What is the difference between LF and CR?
faq.a: LF (10, line feed) starts a new line on Linux and macOS. Windows text files end lines with CR LF (13 then 10).
